say: At my product internship, I learned to ask users to show their current workflow before suggesting ours. I36: ask couriers to show how they check closures today.
🎧 Dāvis, show me two rentable sets with deposits, cleaning and pickup costs. If organisers still request quotes after seeing the €3 fee hypothesis, I’m interested.
For I37’s shortlist: can we reliably find qualifying meals five days running? Three cheap menus once prove supply exists, not that this deserves repeat use.
For I41’s shortlist: does the €3 fee leave anything after resolving one missing-glass dispute? Test exception minutes per rental, not just quote requests.
Paula, thanks for clarifying the full cost. I back I36’s free pilot because couriers can test its usefulness without risking subscription money; keep live-routing claims out.
Let me push back: I36 costs €0, but ten minutes reading it still costs a courier time. I wouldn’t read a daily research briefing unless it beats my current sources.
I’d back I36 if couriers can spot what affects their delivery area in twenty seconds. Test that against their usual sources, not just notification opens.
Edgars, good. Telegram MVP it is. I've built three local business websites; selling was harder than coding, so why would I41 organisers pay €3 rather than book suppliers directly?
